habitat.naturalHabitat: Aquatic environments — brackish water and estuaries
habitat.hostAssociation: Human pathogen; also associates with zooplankton and shellfish in aquatic reservoirs
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Endemic in coastal and estuarine waters, especially in warmer regions
habitat.reservoir: Contaminated water, aquatic reservoirs, asymptomatic human carriers

microscopy.appearance: Gram-negative curved, comma-shaped rods; darting motility on wet mount

culture.media: TCBS (thiosulfate citrate bile salts sucrose) agar
culture.growthCharacteristics: Facultative anaerobe; tolerates alkaline pH, used for selective enrichment in alkaline peptone water
culture.colonyMorphology: Yellow colonies on TCBS agar (sucrose fermenter)

identificationClues: Yellow colonies on TCBS agar — sucrose fermenter
Grows in alkaline conditions such as peptone water enrichment

virulenceFactors: Cholera toxin — an AB toxin that activates adenylate cyclase, causing massive fluid and electrolyte secretion
clinicalImportance.transmission: Fecal-oral route — contaminated water and food
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: Endemic in parts of South Asia and sub-Saharan Africa; capable of explosive epidemic or pandemic spread, especially after disasters disrupting clean water access
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Darting motility plus growth on TCBS selective media allow rapid presumptive identification in outbreak settings

examFacts.importantTest: TCBS agar (yellow colonies); darting motility on wet mount
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Comma-shaped, highly motile rod that produces cholera toxin
